extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students in algebra and number theory studying finite fields, Galois theory, and ramification
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and foundational results about finite fields, their classification and Galois groups, and ramification/inertia/decomposition theory in number fields including Frobenius elements and Chebotarev density. Intended as a compact reference/lecture-style summary with examples and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite field order is a prime power
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite field F must have order p^n, where p is a prime (the characteristic) and n is a positive integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: characteristic is nonzero and hence a prime p; F contains a copy of F_p and is a finite-dimensional vector space over F_p, so |F| = p^n. Examples: F_p has p elements; F_9 ≅ F_3[X]/(X^2+1) has 3^2 elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic of a field (if nonzero) is prime
rubrics_metrics.description: If a field F has nonzero characteristic n, then n must be prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction: if n = a b with 1 < a,b < n then (1+...+1)_a and (1+...+1)_b are nonzero zero-divisors, contradicting field property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freshman's dream in characteristic p
rubrics_metrics.description: In any field of characteristic p, (a + b)^p = a^p + b^p for all a,b in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the binomial theorem and the fact that binomial coefficients (p choose i) are divisible by p for 0<i<p. Exercise: verify the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fermat's little theorem for finite fields
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite field F of order p^n, every x in F satisfies x^{p^n} = x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x ≠ 0, use Lagrange on multiplicative group to get x^{p^n-1} = 1. This implies x^{p^n} - x has all elements of F as roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification: finite fields are unique splitting fields
rubrics_metrics.description: A field F has p^n elements iff F is (isomorphic to) the splitting field of x^{p^n} - x over F_p; for each p^n there is a unique field up to isomorphism denoted F_{p^n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show polynomial x^{p^n}-x has distinct roots (derivative = -1) and its roots form the finite field. Example: factorization of x^9-x modulo 3 shows the 9-element field's roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois group of F_{p^n}/F_p is cyclic generated by Frobenius
rubrics_metrics.description: For F_{p^n}/F_p, Gal(F_{p^n}/F_p) is cyclic of order n generated by the p-th power map σ_p: x ↦ x^p (the Frobenius automorphism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: σ_p is a field automorphism fixing F_p; applying σ_p repeatedly gives x↦x^{p^k}, and σ_p^n = id while smaller powers are not identity because otherwise x^{p^k}-x would have too many roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplicative group of a finite field is cyclic
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite field F of order q, the multiplicative group F^× is cyclic of order q-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Idea: use structure theorem for finite abelian groups. Example: F_{17}^× is cyclic of order 16; exactly half of nonzero elements are quadratic residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: ramified, inert, and split primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a rational prime p and factorization p·O_K = p_1^{e1} · ... · p_g^{eg} in OK, p is: ramified if some e_i>1; inert if g=1 and e_1=1 (i.e., (p) remains prime); split if g>1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in Z[i]: (2) ramified, (3) inert, (5) splits. Use pictorial and factorization examples to build intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inertial degree and ramification index and degree relation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each prime ideal p_i above p, define ramification index e_i and inertial degree f_i by N(p_i) = p^{f_i}. Then the field degree satisfies [K:Q] = Σ_{i=1}^g e_i f_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive from taking norms of both sides of p·O_K factorization: p^{[K:Q]} = Π N(p_i)^{e_i} = Π p^{f_i e_i}. Examples: in Z[i], splitting/inert cases illustrate f values 1 or 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ramification detected by discriminant
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational prime p ramifies in a number field K iff p divides the discriminant Δ_K. For monogenic rings OK = Z[θ], ramification corresponds to f having a double root modulo p (Δ(f) ≡ 0 mod p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: K=Q(i) with Δ_K = -4 implies only p=2 ramifies. Reason: discriminant vanishing modulo p signals double root of minimal polynomial mod p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois extensions: uniform e and f across primes
rubrics_metrics.description: If K/Q is Galois, then in the factorization p·O_K = ∏ p_i^{e_i} the ramification indices e_i are all equal and the inertial degrees f_i are all equal, so p·O_K = (p_1 ··· p_g)^e and [K:Q] = e f g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses transitive action of Gal(K/Q) on primes above p and isomorphisms OK/p ≅ OK/σ(p). Examples contrast Galois and non-Galois (e.g., splitting behavior in cubic non-Galois vs its Galois closure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition group D_p and inertia group I_p
rubrics_metrics.description: For a chosen prime p above rational p, the decomposition group D_p = {σ ∈ Gal(K/Q) | σ(p) = p} is the stabilizer of p. The inertia group I_p is the kernel of the natural map θ: D_p → Gal(OK/p / F_p) and has order e (the ramification index).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties: θ is surjective; if p is unramified, D_p ≅ Gal(OK/p / F_p) ≅ Z/fZ. The inertia group captures ramification; examples and subgroup/field diagrams illustrate decomposition/inertia towers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness of Frobenius element (unramified primes)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p is unramified in a Galois extension K/Q and p is a choice of prime above p, there is a unique element Frob_p ∈ Gal(K/Q) such that for all α ∈ O_K, Frob_p(α) ≡ α^p (mod p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frob_p corresponds (via the isomorphism θ) to the x ↦ x^p map on OK/p ≅ F_{p^f}. Uniqueness is crucial: verifying the functional equation on generators suffices. Example: in Z[i], Frob_p is id for p≡1 (mod4) and complex conjugation for p≡3 (mod4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of Frobenius equals inertial degree
rubrics_metrics.description: The order of Frob_p in Gal(K/Q) equals the inertial degree f_p of the corresponding prime (so Frob_p = id iff p splits completely).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: Frob acts on OK/p ≅ F_{p^f} as x ↦ x^p, which has order f. Use this to read off splitting behavior from Frob's cycle type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugacy class of Frobenius elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For a rational unramified prime p, the set {Frob_p | p runs over primes of K above p} is a conjugacy class in Gal(K/Q). Thus Frob_p is determined up to conjugacy by the rational prime p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If p1 and p2 are primes above p, then Frob_{p2} = σ Frob_{p1} σ^{-1} for any σ with σ(p1)=p2. Example: in S_3 Galois group, the three order-2 Frobenius elements for p correspond to a conjugacy class of type (·)(··).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chebotarev density theorem (over Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a conjugacy class C in G = Gal(K/Q), the density of unramified rational primes p with {Frob_p | primes above p} = C equals |C|/|G|. In particular, every σ ∈ G occurs as Frob_p for infinitely many p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Density means proportion of primes ≤ x tends to |C|/|G| as x→∞, excluding the finitely many ramified primes. Philosophical: Frobenius conjugacy classes are equidistributed in G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic Frobenius identification
rubrics_metrics.description: In the cyclotomic field L = Q(ζ_q), for an unramified rational prime p (p ≠ q), the Frobenius element Frob_p equals the automorphism σ_p sending ζ_q ↦ ζ_q^p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore p splits completely in Q(ζ_q) iff p ≡ 1 (mod q). Use uniqueness of Frobenius and check functional equation on generator ζ_q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility of Frobenius under restriction (functoriality)
rubrics_metrics.description: If L/Q and K/Q are Galois with K ⊆ L, and P above p above p are unramified, then Frob_P restricted to K equals Frob_p (i.e., Frob_P↾K = Frob_p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the natural maps OK/p → OL/P and injectivity of field homomorphisms; diagram commutativity shows the power-of-p action matches downstairs. This is used in arithmetic applications (e.g., quadratic reciprocity argument).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius controls factorization and splitting behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The Frobenius element encapsulates splitting/inert behavior: ord(Frob_p)=1 iff p splits completely; ord(Frob_p)=f indicates inertial degree f; membership of Frob_p in specified subgroups corresponds to splitting in intermediate fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application: in the quadratic reciprocity proof, Frob_p ∈ H (index-2 subgroup) ⇔ p splits in the quadratic subfield ⇔ p is a quadratic residue modulo q. Use restriction and cyclotomic identification to translate congruence conditions into group membership.
